about: The states and territories of late 1850 (after California's admission on September 9), in four plain groups, for a lesson map. Outlines are Esri's digitization of the 1850 plate in Harper's Atlas of American History (1920), a public-domain map in the Library of Congress (loc.gov/item/32005827). The source classes each area by the law that made it free or slave, in 16 classes; this table replaces those with four. To fact-check before version 1.0: every status and admission year; the wording for the territories; what the three small 'Unidentified' areas of the source were in 1850.

units.note: Admitted as a free state under the Missouri Compromise of 1820.

units.basis: Admitted as a free state on September 9, 1850, as part of the Compromise of 1850.

units.note: Includes today's West Virginia, which was part of Virginia until 1863.
Annexed as a slave state in 1845.

Admitted as a slave state under the Missouri Compromise of 1820, although most of it lies north of the compromise line. The source map draws the northwest corner, added in 1837, separately; here it is part of the state.

units.name: District of Columbia
units.basis: Slavery was legal here. The Compromise of 1850 ended the slave trade in the District, but not slavery.

units.name: Minnesota Territory
units.basis: Organized in 1849. Slavery was banned here.

units.name: Unorganized territory
units.basis: Closed to slavery by the Missouri Compromise of 1820, because it lies north of the compromise line.

units.name: Utah Territory
units.basis: Organized by the Compromise of 1850, which left slavery for the settlers to decide.

units.name: New Mexico Territory
units.basis: Organized by the Compromise of 1850, which left slavery for the settlers to decide.

units.name: Indian Territory
units.basis: Not an organized territory. Slavery was legal among several of the nations moved here in the 1830s.
units.note: The source layer labels this area Oklahoma, a name not used in 1850.

units.name: Unorganized land (boundaries unsettled in 1850)
units.basis: Shown as free on the source map (Harper's Atlas of American History, 1920).

units.name: Unorganized land (boundaries unsettled in 1850)
units.basis: Shown as open to slavery on the source map (Harper's Atlas of American History, 1920).
